A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DynamicLimit-Exp study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable, and corresponding material can be matched across revisions and relocations.

before.justification: Sections 4–5 report original GPT-2 training and Zorro evaluations using AO-CHILDES and Wikipedia, including reversed-memory, sentence-length, and embedding analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds intermediate-epoch accuracy trajectories, FILLER.GAP embedding results, and dataset sentence-length distributions.

M1.justification: The proposed method retains the GPT-2 backbone, exponential ALiBi slope update, and working-memory definition in Equations 1–3. v3 omits the explicit shared-slope-across-heads explanation but specifies no alternative procedure, so this establishes a documentation change rather than an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions use English AO-CHILDES and Wikipedia, the same Zorro grammatical categories, and the same four sentence-length conditions. The added developmental and embedding analyses reuse this existing coverage.

E2.justification: The main baselines remain NoLimit, StaticLimit, and DynamicLimit-Linear. Comparator membership also remains unchanged in the corresponding reversed-memory, sentence-length, and CASE embedding comparisons.

E3.justification: Table 6 changes maximum sequence length from 32 for AO-CHILDES and 64 for Wikipedia to an undifferentiated 32; the PDFs do not establish whether experiments were rerun. v3 also introduces accuracy evaluation at epochs 1, 5, and 10 for six categories selected by final-stage significance, and removes variance from the embedding diagnostics.

E4.justification: v3 adds direct developmental accuracy trajectories across six grammatical categories (Section 5.2, Figure 3), extends representation analysis to FILLER.GAP, and adds corpus sentence-length distributions. These substantially expand the developmental analyses. The reversal and sentence-length experiments remain, while the earlier CASE analysis moves to Appendix E with its variance component omitted.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over three seeds. v3 introduces proportion z-tests at p < 0.05 with better/worse significance markers in Tables 1–3 and significance annotations in Table 5. This substantially expands inferential reporting without documenting additional runs. Table 3's new caption reverses the comparison direction indicated by its scores and deltas.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–3 and 5 are retained. Added results concern intermediate-epoch accuracy, FILLER.GAP embedding statistics, and corpus-length distributions. The original CASE entropy and distance values reappear unchanged in v3 Table 7, while its variance values are removed.

T1.justification: The exponential working-memory model and Equations 1–3 remain mathematically equivalent. Appendix D supplies standard entropy and Euclidean centroid-distance formulas for existing analysis measures; it adds calculation explanations without new theoretical results, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The main methodological and accuracy claims remain. The conclusion qualifies the cognitive contribution as a computational plausibility test and hypothesis-generating evidence, explicitly stating that the results do not establish the necessity of working-memory development for human learners.

C2.justification: v3 adds a specific ELLIPSIS limitation: initial memory restrictions may hinder structures requiring substantial context early in learning. It also develops a language-evolution rationale for cognitive constraints and explains the limits of treating language models as cognitive testbeds. These substantially refine mechanism explanations and applicability boundaries; the existing scalability and English-only limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds a CPLM repository link, identifies the Transformers implementation, reports RTX A5000 hardware and approximately one hour per run, specifies reversed-schedule parameters, and documents histogram and centroid-distance calculations. However, v1's explicit statement that DynamicLimit-Exp shares its slope across attention heads is omitted.

R1.justification: The research positioning expands substantially through separate L1/L2 discussions, efficient-communication literature, and cognitive reverse-engineering perspectives, including Dupoux and Warstadt–Bowman. The comparison with Constantinescu emphasizes development during the critical period versus later plasticity constraints. Constantinescu's publication-year update concerns the same previously cited work.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, analytical discussion, and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting. Terminology and section titles change, the analysis gains a developmental-trajectory section, and the appendices are reorganized from A–B to A–E, including relocation of existing CASE and Zorro material.

P2.justification: v3 adds six-panel accuracy trajectories, FILLER.GAP scatterplots, and sentence-length histograms; relocates the original CASE visualization and summary to the appendix; and removes variance columns. Significance annotations and revised captions accompany substantial rearrangement of the main-text and appendix displays.

improvement.justification: The added learning trajectories, statistical reporting, explicit ellipsis limitation, cautious human-learning conclusion, and reproducibility details make v3 easier to assess. The core accuracy results remain unchanged. The net gain is limited by Table 3's reversed significance explanation, the unexplained sequence-length revision, and removal of the shared-slope specification.
